title: Protection & Switchgear
summary: Fault types and symmetrical components, relay types and where they are used, CT/PT rules, breaker media, arresters and earthing. Numericals: fault current, fault MVA, PSM, breaking capacity.
definitions: Any unbalanced 3-phase set = positive + negative + zero sequence sets (Fortescue).
Plug setting multiplier = fault current in relay ÷ relay setting current.
Time multiplier setting; operating time scales linearly with TMS.
Inverse definite minimum time: inverse at low multiples, definite minimum at high currents.
Transient voltage across breaker contacts just after current zero (RRRV = its rate of rise).
Power-frequency voltage across contacts after final arc extinction.
Arc-suppression reactor between neutral and earth tuned to line capacitance.
Off-load disconnecting switch for visible isolation; operated only after the breaker opens.
formulas: PSM = I_fault × (CT sec/CT pri) / (setting% × CT sec)
facts: Most common fault: single line-to-ground (≈70–80%). Most severe (usually): 3-phase symmetrical. Only 3-phase fault is symmetrical.
Zero-sequence current needs a ground path; it cannot flow in lines feeding a delta or an ungrounded star.
L–L fault: no zero sequence. L–G: sequence networks in series.
Distance relays protect lines: mho for long lines (inherently directional, least affected by power swing), reactance for short lines (immune to arc resistance), impedance for medium.
Differential (Merz–Price) protection for transformers, generators, busbars; percentage bias for CT mismatch; 2nd-harmonic restraint for inrush.
Directional overcurrent relays for ring mains and parallel feeders.
Never open-circuit a CT secondary under load (dangerous high voltage, core saturation). CT secondary 1 A or 5 A; VT secondary 110 V.
SF6: electronegative, 2–3× air dielectric strength, used at EHV. Vacuum CB: 11–33 kV, arc in metal vapour. Air-blast: older EHV.
AC arcs are interrupted at current zero.
Surge arresters: line to earth; modern ones are gapless metal-oxide (ZnO). Shield wire protects against direct strokes (≈30° shielding angle).
Arcing grounds occur in ungrounded systems; suppressed by Petersen coil.
Earth resistance target: ≈0.5 Ω power stations, ≈1 Ω large substations. 30 mA RCD protects persons.
Generator: reverse power relay (motoring), negative-sequence relay (unbalance heats rotor), loss-of-excitation relay.
About 80% of overhead-line faults are transient → auto-reclosing.
traps: I_f for L–G is 3I_a0 — don't stop at I_a0.
PSM must include the relay percentage setting (125% of 5 A = 6.25 A).
Breaking MVA uses √3 × kV × kA — not 3 × kV × kA.
Mho relay is for LONG lines, reactance relay for SHORT lines.

examples.q: E = 1 p.u., Z1 = Z2 = j0.2, Z0 = j0.1 (solidly grounded). Find L–G, L–L and 3-phase fault currents.
